title: What is API (Hindi)
observations: The sampled slides use a restaurant intermediary analogy, then show website/mobile clients connecting to an application and database. API release policies appear on the introductory slide.
alignment: Keep the runnable introduction, but explain that it is an added exercise: the sampled lecture sections are conceptual slides, not a Django implementation.

title: What is Web API (Hindi)
observations: The slides trace the client request through a Web API to a web application/database and the response back to the client. Later slides introduce API registration and an API key/token.
alignment: Add an explicit request/response walkthrough. Explain that the slide's query-string key is an illustration; this collection uses Authorization headers in the authentication lessons.

title: What is REST and REST API (Hindi)
observations: The sampled slides use students as the resource, distinguish a collection URL from a student-specific URL, and map GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE to those endpoints.
alignment: Keep student-resource names and add the collection/detail method table to the lesson notes. Explain that the introductory project demonstrates GET and later projects implement all methods.

title: Django Rest Framework and How to Install Uninstall Django Rest Framework (Hindi)
observations: The installation demonstration visibly uses Django 3.1.1 and djangorestframework 3.11.1, with a pip uninstall demonstration. Introductory slides discuss browsable APIs and serialization.
alignment: Document the observed historical versions alongside the collection's tested Django 5.2 and DRF 3.16. Keep installation isolated in a virtual environment.

title: Download Django REST Framework Study Material (Hindi)
observations: The reviewed frames show the instructor's study-material page and a purchase/download flow for a PPT-and-code bundle. This is not a Django coding demonstration.
alignment: Label this folder as a companion reference exercise. Do not imply its generated code is the instructor's downloadable bundle.

title: Serializer and Serializertion in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: A slide explicitly defines StudentSerializer using Serializer with name, roll and city fields. A later code frame shows a separate myapp.py client using requests.get against a stuinfo detail URL and printing student dictionaries.
alignment: Simplify this serialization-only serializer and add a standalone HTTP client plus stuinfo aliases. Keep the existing collection URLs for compatibility.

title: Serializer Fields and Core Arguments in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The reviewed slides include CharField, UUIDField, and the core arguments initial, style, allow_null and source. The original companion covered only a subset of these fields.
alignment: Add a runnable field playground covering these arguments without adding irrelevant database columns. Explain form initial values separately from input defaults.

title: DeSerialization and Insert Data Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The code sections show a create method and a student_create function reading request.body through io.BytesIO and JSONParser, validating a serializer, saving it, and rendering a response with JSONRenderer. A separate client prepares a student dictionary.
alignment: Add a raw Django create endpoint demonstrating that explicit pipeline, before the later request.data abstraction. Retain CSRF and meaningful error status codes.

title: CRUD API using Function Based View and Class Based View in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The sampled code uses myapp.py helper functions including get_data and update_data. The server serializes a student queryset with many=True. The class-based section defines StudentAPI(View) and visibly disables CSRF on dispatch.
alignment: Add a client with similarly named helpers and use the explicit JSONParser pipeline. Explain the intentional difference: keep CSRF enabled and put record ids in detail URLs rather than GET bodies.

title: Validation in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The sampled serializer shows object-level name/city validation using Ranchi, and a reusable start_with_r validator. A response displays a roll-field validation failure.
alignment: Add separate reusable, field-level and object-level practice rules. Use startswith rather than indexing the first character, and preserve existing values during partial validation.

title: Model Serializer in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The first code sample uses ModelSerializer with Meta.model and explicit name/roll/city fields. Later samples add object-level validation, demonstrating that inferred fields do not prevent custom rules.
alignment: Keep the explicit ModelSerializer and explain that custom validation can be added without writing default create/update methods.

title: Function Based API View in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The sampled function-view code validates request.data and returns Response objects, with a later example explicitly returning HTTP_201_CREATED. StudentAdmin shows id/name/roll/city columns. An intermediate update uses partial=True with PUT.
alignment: Add readable admin columns and document the deliberate PUT/PATCH distinction in this companion. Existing function views already demonstrate the main abstractions.

title: Class Based APIView in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: StudentAPI inherits APIView, handles an optional pk for retrieval, and uses request.data in post. Later samples show the browsable API's update forms.
alignment: Keep explicit APIView methods. Explain that the companion separates collection and detail classes instead of branching on optional pk in one class.

title: Generic API View and Mixins in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The reviewed code defines individual StudentUpdate and StudentDestroy classes using GenericAPIView plus mixins, with HTTP handlers delegating to update/retrieve actions.
alignment: Add individually routed mixin examples alongside the existing combined collection/detail classes so the build-up remains visible.

title: Concrete View Class in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The lecture shows separate StudentList, StudentCreate and StudentRetrieve classes before combined ListCreateAPIView and RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView classes. URL examples switch between the variants.
alignment: Add single-operation concrete views with separate practice URLs, preserving the existing combined CRUD endpoint.

title: ViewSet in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The code defines StudentViewSet with list, retrieve and create actions, registers it with DefaultRouter, and displays viewset metadata such as action and basename in the terminal.
alignment: Keep explicit viewset actions and add notes mapping HTTP methods to router action names. The companion uses get_object_or_404 for missing ids.

title: Model View Set and Ready Only Model View Set in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The samples show student admin columns, a writable browsable API form, and a read-only detail response whose allowed methods are GET, HEAD and OPTIONS.
alignment: Keep both writable and read-only endpoints and explain the visible Allow-header distinction.

title: Basic Authentication and Permission Class in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The samples show BasicAuthentication and IsAuthenticated on StudentModelViewSet, plus global authentication/permission settings as an alternative.
alignment: The main route already matches this structure. Added practice routes compare public, authenticated, staff and Django-model permission policies.

title: Session Authentication and Permission in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The code uses SessionAuthentication and shows alternative permission classes, including DjangoModelPermissions; a slide explains authenticated-or-read-only access.
alignment: Added runnable permission comparisons. Session writes retain CSRF protection; IsAdminUser checks is_staff.

title: Custom Permission in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The code moves from SessionAuthentication/IsAuthenticated to an imported MyPermission class. The sampled frames do not show that custom class's implementation.
alignment: The companion's IsStaffOrReadOnly is an explicitly original policy, not a reconstruction of the unseen MyPermission body.

title: Authentication and Permission in Function Based View in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The function student_api uses api_view for CRUD and adds authentication_classes([BasicAuthentication]) and permission_classes([IsAuthenticated]) decorators.
alignment: The existing companion already uses these decorators. Read their order and compare function views with class attributes in lesson 18.

title: Token Authentication in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The samples show a token in Django admin, a gettoken route using obtain_auth_token, an HTTPie introduction, and a token-authenticated PUT request.
alignment: Added the lecture-named /gettoken/ alias. The original /api/token/ remains. Notes include HTTPie examples with a placeholder instead of a copied credential.

title: Custom Authentication in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: CustomAuthentication subclasses BaseAuthentication, reads request.GET['username'] via get, finds a User and returns (user, None); missing or unknown values follow different paths.
alignment: Added a from-scratch CustomAuthentication exercise that verifies a secret database token. Username-only identity is not sufficient authentication; the runnable code intentionally differs.

title: JSON Web Token and Simple JWT in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The slides show access/refresh lifetimes. Routes named gettoken, refreshtoken and verifytoken use Simple JWT views; the viewset uses JWTAuthentication and IsAuthenticated.
alignment: Added the three lecture-named aliases, preserving /api/token/ routes. Tokens retain the Bearer header scheme.

title: Throttling in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The sampled responses show HTTP 429 with Retry-After, and the lecture switches from a viewset to individual generic view routes.
alignment: Existing throttles demonstrate the limit. Explain that rates/cache scope are companion choices, since those settings are not visible in these samples.

title: Filtering and django filter in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: Samples show student responses with a passby field and a ListAPIView with filterset_fields=['city'].
alignment: The companion filters city and roll. Its Student model has no passby field; that is a deliberate smaller schema, not a copied model definition.

title: Search Filter in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The view uses SearchFilter and search_fields=['city']; the browser requests a search for Bokaro and shows matching students.
alignment: The companion searches both name and city, an explicit extension. Compare ?search=Ranchi with exact filtering from lesson 26.

title: Ordering Filter in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The OrderingFilter slide lists several ordering_fields choices. The final sampled view restricts ordering to name, and browser samples use descending ordering.
alignment: The companion explicitly permits name, roll and id. A minus sign requests descending order; the extra allowed fields are an extension.

title: Page Number Pagination in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: MyPageNumberPagination has page_size=5, then page_query_param='p' and page_size_query_param='records'. A slide covers maximum page size and last-page strings.
alignment: Added a practice endpoint with p/records and page size 5. The cap of 10 is our bounded companion setting; the original route retains page/page_size.

title: Limit Offset Pagination in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: MyLimitOffsetPagination is selected by pagination_class. The final sample sets default_limit=5, mylimit/myoffset query names and max_limit=3.
alignment: Added the same query names, with default_limit=3 and max_limit=3 so the default does not exceed the cap. Main route retains limit/offset.

title: Cursor Pagination in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The slides explain cursor ordering. A sample shows page_size=3 followed by a missing-created-field error; the last frame shows next/previous cursor URLs.
alignment: Added a size-3 practice variant using stable id ordering. The sampled final ordering assignment is not visible; do not assume it matches ours.

title: Serializer Relations in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The code uses Singer/Song, singer/song router prefixes, a reverse song field, StringRelatedField and a read-only SlugRelatedField using duration.
alignment: Added singer/song models, admin columns, CRUD, seed data and four relation representations. The earlier classroom exercise remains available.

title: Hyperlinked Model Serializer in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: StudentSerializer subclasses HyperlinkedModelSerializer. A shell repr shows a url HyperlinkedIdentityField referring to student-detail alongside id/name/roll/city.
alignment: The existing companion demonstrates the same URL representation. Inspect serializer repr and router basename together.

title: Nested Serializer in Django REST Framework (Hindi)
observations: The lecture again uses Singer/Song and singer/song routes. The last response nests song dictionaries under a singer's sungby key.
alignment: Added an original singer/song nested-output example. It uses the reverse key song consistently with lesson 32 instead of the visible sungby key; nested writes remain explicit separate requests.

title: Django API Project and How to Disable Browsable API in Production (Hindi)
observations: A diagram connects an existing CRUD website and database to an API. UserSerializer imports enroll.models.User. Later frames show the HTML enrollment form/table and /api/crud/ JSON, including plaintext password values.
alignment: Added an existing enroll app with HTML CRUD and a REST endpoint using the same model. Passwords are hashed and write-only, and access is staff-only. The earlier JWT student capstone is an additional exercise, not the lecture's exact app.
